key_insight: A two-stage data-driven atomistic modeling pipeline can capture how amino-silane passivation interacts with hybrid halide perovskite surfaces as molecular coverage increases.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical route to design and optimize perovskite surface passivation strategies for improved solar-cell stability and optoelectronic performance.
method: Build a large open training set of diverse metal and hybrid halide perovskite structures (hyP-26).
Fine-tune on a small, specialized dataset for amino-silane adsorbed on the perovskite surface.
Use the trained model to simulate coverage-dependent collective behavior at a mixed-composition perovskite surface.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a multistep training pipeline validated by application to experimentally realistic surface-passivation scenarios and a coverage-dependent surface study.
watch_item: Performance may depend strongly on the quality and representativeness of the curated general dataset and the small specialized fine-tuning set.
paper_title: Data-driven atomistic modelling of hybrid halide perovskite passivation
